summary: Edge AI engineer who turns research models into real-time systems on embedded hardware: compressing, quantizing and accelerating networks until they fit a device's latency and memory budget, then building them into robots that act on what they see. M.S. Computer Engineering, RIT (2026).

experience.title: AI/ML Intern
bullets: Fine-tuned DONUT, an OCR-free document-understanding transformer, on a custom medical-billing dataset for structured field extraction, adding domain-specific tokens and resizing the decoder embeddings.
Raised validation accuracy from 55% to 93% through improved preprocessing and model tuning.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Trained YOLOv8n on 1,133 curated, annotated images to 83% mAP@50 for toothbrush health classification, and exported it to ONNX and TFLite for mobile deployment.

experience.title: Research Intern (Capstone)
bullets: Raised stitching quality to a PSNR of 86 with a custom alpha-blended wavelet bank (sym6 + bior3.5), optimized homography stitching and concurrency, up from 65 with a bit-manipulation baseline.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — M.S. Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated faster-whisper speech-to-text (1.0–1.4 s), Gemini intent classification (<500 ms) and TensorRT-optimized YOLO for visual servoing, accelerating detection 5.2× over eager PyTorch (56.7 → 10.9 ms, 17.6 → 92 FPS).
Drove the system to 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5 s voice-to-pick by hardening it against false-positive detections, servo brown-out and stale-frame capture.

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Reduced GPU memory by ~55% with 8-bit quantization (bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) on TinyLlama 1.1B, profiling peak VRAM and latency across prompt types with pynvml and psutil.
Held accuracy within 1% across HellaSwag, GSM8K and ARC with only +0.09 perplexity: near-lossless compression for edge deployment.

projects.name: Quantization-Aware Training for Integer-Only Inference
bullets: Implemented quantization-aware training in PyTorch for a bias-free 256-64-10 MLP with straight-through-estimator fake quantization, per-layer symmetric int8 weights and uint8 activations; integer-only inference reaches 97.43% on the MNIST test set.
Calibrated the hidden-activation scale with an EMA observer and froze it for the final 25% of training so the weights adapt to the deployed scale.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced VGG16's convolution layers with custom CUDA C++ kernels (memory coalescing, constant memory, preallocated buffers): 49.2 ms vs 73.3 ms for a naive GPU kernel and 77.5 ms on CPU, ~35% faster with identical accuracy.
